_doc: Which rinexqc result fields may change when a file is converted by rinexconv, and how (PLAN.md rev. 4 §5.1 item 4; docs/QC_METRICS.md §7 gate E3). Written in Q0a from the specs, the loss table (tests/expectations/allowed_losses.json) and the converter's report categories (rinexconv/report.py: losses, repairs, normalisations, assumptions; plus the rule and warning names that change data), before any rinexqc code. The Q1 test runs rinexqc on a file and on each rinexconv conversion of it, with the same inputs, and compares: every metric in 'physical' must be equal on the scopes both results hold; any other difference must be allowed by an entry below for a category present in that conversion's report. A category the report holds that this file does not list fails the test: a new converter category needs an entry here first.
status: v0, Q0a, 2026-11-06 (revised after review rounds 1 and 2): signed off by the user with Q1's gates on 2026-11-06; frozen with the commit that records it

comparison.inputs: Both runs get the same inputs (the same nav companion, --glo-fcn, --overrides, SNR receiver table) and the same options. If the source can be read only with --lenient, both runs use --lenient, so lenient_read is true in both. A difference caused only by an input or option one run lacked is a test error, not an allowed change. When a conversion drops GLONASS SLOT / FRQ #, the target run gets the source's channels as --glo-fcn, so both runs know the same channels.
comparison.epochs: Data epochs are matched by time, after the shift a 'time' effect below names (OBS.TIME-SYSTEM.BDT-TO-GPS: +14 s).
comparison.signals: Scopes are matched by the adapter's canonical signal key (QC_METRICS §1.2): '<system>:<code>' with the RINEX 3/4 code (band digits normalised, so OBS.BDS-B1I-BAND needs no entry) or the RINEX 2 code ('G:C1', 'G:P1', 'G:P2'; never merged), and '#2' for a second column. RINEX 2 -> 3/4: each source key maps to the target code named by the report's obs-code-attribute assumption (detail 'C2->C2X', 'P2->C2W'). RINEX 3/4 -> 2: each source code named by a rule OBS.V3V2.CODEMAP.<sys>.<code> maps to the 2-character code rinexconv.codemap.v3_to_v2 gives for it (tests may use rinexconv: PLAN §3.9); where several source codes map to one target code, the obs-code-collapsed loss says which was kept and the others are 'absent'. RINEX 3/4 <-> 3/4: the same code, after band normalisation.
comparison.scopes: The source run is restricted with --select to the systems and signals the target holds (QC_SCHEMA §1), so every per-scope value, file-level aggregate and detector (whose common estimates are medians over satellites) is computed on identical support in both runs. A scope present in one result only must still be explained by an 'absent' effect; removing it from the source run is what --select does for the comparison.
comparison.reals: Integers and classes exactly. Reals within 1e-9 relative (or 1e-12 absolute near zero), unless an effect gives a bound. Under a category with a bound: (1) a detector event may be present in one run only if its test statistic in the other run is within the propagated bound of the threshold (the test computes the margin); (2) a value that the rounding brings to exactly 0.000 becomes missing, so counts, coverage, arcs and detector support may change at exactly those observations, which the test finds from the source values.
comparison.out_of_scope: Conversions with several inputs (--merge) and refusals; the invariance test covers single-file conversions that end converted, converted-with-assumptions or converted-with-removal.
comparison.support_changes: Retired: with the source run restricted by --select (comparison.scopes), systems, codes or channels removed by the conversion no longer change detector support, so their 'support' effects below hold only for an unrestricted run (a user comparing results by hand).

change_kinds.none: No QC field may change because of this category.
change_kinds.absent: The named scopes are absent from the target result (the data are gone).
change_kinds.value: The named values may change, as 'how' says, within 'bound' when given.
change_kinds.unit: The unit may change from 'from' to 'to'; the numbers stay equal.
change_kinds.status: The status may change from 'from' to 'to'.
change_kinds.support: Support counts may decrease (or increase, if 'how' says so); values computed on what remains must still agree where both are testable.
change_kinds.time: Epoch times shift by 'shift_s'; values that are times shift with them; durations, counts and differences do not change.
change_kinds.provenance: Only provenance and header-echo fields change.

always_differ.how: the validator's findings on the target are those the conversion report lists as inherited (VAL.INHERITED); every other source finding may disappear

derived_rules._doc: Two adapter rules that make metrics invariant where raw fields change (docs/QC_METRICS.md §1.2 and §4.1)
derived_rules.half-cycle: obs.avail.flags counts a canonical half-cycle observation as: RINEX 2, a GPS L1/L2 phase whose effective wavelength factor that epoch is 2 (the header or event factor, flipped by LLI bit 1), and any other phase with LLI bit 1 ([P8], an interpretation: rinexconv copies bit 1 there verbatim); RINEX 3/4, a phase with LLI bit 1. The raw bit-1 counts are reported beside it.
derived_rules.overflow-clip: overflow-clip-candidate: LLI bit 0 and a phase change of 1e9 cycles to within 1e7 cycles; a subset of lost-lock, which keeps counting it (QC_METRICS §1.2).

rule_or_warning_doc: Every rule and warning name the converter records (rinexconv/*.py, rinexcore/*.py: .rule() and .warn() calls, listed 2026-11-06), '*' for a name built from values. Most carry no effect of their own; they are listed so that the Q1 test can fail on a name that is not here. A name listed under repair (NAV.GLO.TK-DAY-BASIS, NAV.HDR.TIMECORR.LAYOUT) also covers its use as a warning. The validator's own finding names (VAL.*) are not report entries: they fall under always_differ (compliance).
